title: Horae beatae Mariae virginis (use of Paris)
shelf_note: No tradition or collection given in the packet. An illuminated Paris-use Book of Hours is a devotional primary source; nothing on these pages contradicts the title.
structure_note: No structure counts given. Pencilled folio/page numbers in the lower-left margin read 35 (p.5), 57 (p.10) and 85 (p.14), rising in order. None of the three pages has a translation (translation is null on all of them), so a reader sees only the Latin/French transcription. The metadata says 'published 1515', but the pages look like a hand-illuminated manuscript in a bâtarde hand, so the date may be an estimate rather than an imprint (not checkable from these pages).

other.note: No translation exists for this page (translation null), so the Latin versicle 'Domine labia mea aperies…' on the scroll is not rendered in English.

book_verdict: The transcriptions are faithful on all three miniature pages. The short scroll texts are read correctly, the pseudo-lettering in the frieze is rightly flagged as decorative, and the scene descriptions match the images. The only gaps are that no page has a translation and that p.10's pencilled page number is missing.
